Subject: Questions on CCPA/CPRA classification and telemetry handling

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — appreciated the performance numbers. Our legal team raised a couple of follow ups on the privacy side before we can move to procurement:

1) Classification: Will Redwood sign an addendum that explicitly identifies Redwood as a "service provider" (or processor) under CCPA/CPRA and state privacy addenda? We need the language for our template.

2) Telemetry & logs: We need assurance that any telemetry, logs, or derived usage metrics are not "sold" under CCPA and are not used for targeted advertising. In addition, can you confirm default retention for request-level logs and any forensic traces (IP, query text) and whether that can be shortened?

3) Subprocessors: please provide a short list of subprocessors used for routing/caching and whether any are offshore. If you have an onshore fallback option that could be contractually enforced, that's preferred for us.

I've attached Greenline's security questionnaire and will loop in our procurement/legal if the answers match our risk profile.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that's faster.

Best,

Samantha — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Quick answers up front, details below and a draft addendum attached.

- Classification: Redwood will sign addenda that reflect a service provider / processor role for customer-controlled data. The attached DP Addendum v3 includes explicit language that mirrors CPRA service provider definitions and limits use to performance of services.

- Telemetry & logs: Redwood does not "sell" customer data or telemetry. Telemetry collected for operational purposes (routing, caching, abuse detection, anonymized performance metrics) is treated as service-related and not used for advertising or resale. Default retention for request-level logs is 30 days; we can offer a configurable 7/30/90-day option depending on customer tier and retention controls. We can provide a CSV extract documenting deletion timestamps on request for audits.

- Subprocessors: We use a small set of infrastructure and monitoring vendors; most are cloud-hosted providers in the US with a limited set of global CDN/cache nodes. We maintain an onshore fallback plan for telemetry routing; details are in the DP Addendum appendix. If Greenline requires strict onshore-only subprocessors, we can discuss a scoped carve-out (may impact latency/cost).

Next steps I propose: 1) Attach DP Addendum v3 (marked for negotiation); 2) Neha can propose precise contract wording for the telemetry retention clause and onshore fallback; 3) If acceptable, we can send a DocuSign for procurement.

Attached: Redwood_DPAddendum_v3.pdf; SOC2-summary.pdf

Happy to schedule a quick call with our security/legal team.

Thanks,

Hi Samantha / Michael — looping in legal. A few suggested contract-level edits that would address Greenline's concerns without opening undue operational exposure: 

1) Add explicit service-provider clause: "Redwood shall act solely as a Service Provider (as defined under CPRA) and shall not sell Personal Information. Redwood's use of Personal Information shall be limited to performing the services specified in the Agreement."

2) Telemetry retention clause: offer tiers where default is 30 days, with a contractual option for 7-day retention for request-level logs. Include an audit mechanism: upon customer request Redwood will provide a time-stamped deletion report (CSV) and a redacted sample demonstrating sanitization.

3) Subprocessor/onshore fallback: propose an appendix listing current subprocessors and an onshore-fallback SLA (e.g., 48-hour failover to US-only routing for queries originating from customer-controlled regions). If Greenline requires contractually bound onshore-only subprocessors, mark as "scope-limiting change" and note potential performance/cost impact.

If these are acceptable language-wise I can draft a short addendum (2 pages) for DocuSign. Michael / Aditya: what is the typical turnaround for a customer DP addendum to move from signed to enforcement (analytics-friendly question: do we need 2-3 weeks to set retention flags and telemetry pipelines)?

— Neha
